topic.angle: A knotted rope makes a right angle

card.title: Knots, ropes and a right angle

panels.text: Ancient Egypt had rope stretchers, surveyors who marked land and building foundations with knotted cords pulled tight so they did not sag.
They used 3-4-5 triangles. Why that triple? Because 3 squared plus 4 squared is 9 + 16 = 25, which is 5 squared.
A triangle whose sides are a Pythagorean triple like (3, 4, 5) is a right triangle. The right angle sits between the sides of length 3 and 4.
So a loop of rope knotted into 12 equal spaces, pulled taut into 3, 4 and 5, gives a perfect corner. Modern surveyors still use the trick.

probes.question: Which set of side lengths makes a right triangle?
True or false: in a 3-4-5 triangle, the right angle is between the sides of length 3 and 4.

claims.quote: a surveyor who measured real property demarcations and foundations using knotted cords , stretched so the rope did not sag

claims.claim: They used 3-4-5 triangles, still used by modern surveyors
claims.quote: Rope stretchers used 3-4-5 triangles and the plummet , which are still in use by modern surveyors.

claims.claim: A triangle whose sides are a Pythagorean triple is a right triangle (so 3-4-5 is right, right angle between 3 and 4)
claims.quote: A triangle whose side lengths are a Pythagorean triple is a right triangle
claims.note: Which sides meet at the right angle follows from 5 being the hypotenuse in a^2 + b^2 = c^2. The page does not describe the 12-knot loop itself; that is derived from the same maths.
